answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation that accrues slowly: an agent earns trust only by completing verified work over time, like a sonnet built line by line rather than shouted all at once. A fresh identity starts in a dim lagoon of low trust, and only consistent, useful behavior lights its lantern brighter. Sybils can spawn a thousand names, but they cannot fake months of earned history, so cheap copies stay dim while real agents shine.
